h: Temples with a message and a famous gardener
p: Stowe was created by the Temple family, Viscounts Cobham, who used the landscape to make political and philosophical points. Many of the temples and monuments carry hidden meanings, which makes the gardens a puzzle as well as a pleasure. The Temple of British Worthies, for example, displays busts of figures from history and the arts that the family admired.

A young Lancelot Brown, later known as Capability Brown, worked here as head gardener early in his career, before going on to shape some of the most famous landscapes in England. Walking around Stowe, you can spot the beginnings of his natural style.

Look out for the Palladian Bridge, which you can walk across, the Gothic Temple standing on its hill, and the Elysian Fields, a gentle valley with temples set around a stream. Each corner of the gardens has a different feel, so it rarely becomes repetitive.

Visitors arrive through the New Inn, a restored 18th-century inn that once welcomed the earliest tourists to Stowe. It is a nice reminder that people have been coming to admire these gardens for nearly three hundred years.

Nearby, Silverstone, home of the British Grand Prix, is just a few miles away and has an interactive museum about British motor racing. Buckingham's Old Gaol, a quirky little building in the town centre, is also worth a look, and the market town has places for a bite after your walk.
